l:akkusativ:0:body: These prepositions (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, entlang) always require the accusative case. With entlang the noun often precedes the preposition, e.g., den Fluss entlang.
l:akkusativ:0:ex1: The gift is für meinen Bruder.
l:akkusativ:0:title: The Fixed Accusative Prepositions
l:akkusativ:1:body: In the accusative, the definite articles are den (masculine), die (feminine), das (neuter), and die (plural). The personal pronouns are mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie.
l:akkusativ:1:title: Articles and Pronouns
l:akkusativ:2:body: The prepositions für, gegen, bis, and um take the accusative case. Für indicates purpose or a time span, gegen expresses an approximate time or contrast, bis marks a limit, and um denotes a location around something or a specific time.
l:akkusativ:2:ex0: I am studying for the exam.
l:akkusativ:2:ex2: The children sit around the table.
l:akkusativ:2:title: Time, Purpose, and Direction
l:akkusativ:3:body: The preposition ohne never takes the dative; it requires the accusative (e.g., ohne den Regenschirm, not ohne dem Regenschirm). With für, the article agrees with the noun's gender and case (e.g., für meinen Vater, für meine Mutter).
l:akkusativ:3:title: Common Mistakes
l:akkusativ:intro: Accusative prepositions always require the accusative case. They indicate direction, purpose, contrast, duration, or lack of accompaniment.
l:dativ:0:body: The most important are mit, nach, aus, bei, von, zu, seit, and gegenüber. They never change case: even with movement they stay in the dative.
l:dativ:0:title: Fixed Dative Prepositions
l:dativ:1:body: In the dative case, the definite article is "dem" for masculine and neuter, "der" for feminine, and "den" for plural. The personal pronouns are "mir", "dir", "ihm", "ihr", "ihm", "uns", "euch", "ihnen".
l:dativ:1:ex2: The book belongs to the children.
l:dativ:1:title: Articles and Pronouns in the Dative
l:dativ:2:body: Prepositions often merge with the definite article: "zu" + "dem" = "zum", "zu" + "der" = "zur", "von" + "dem" = "vom", "bei" + "dem" = "beim". These forms are standard, not colloquial.
l:dativ:2:title: Contractions with the Article
l:dativ:3:body: After these prepositions the accusative is wrong. Also note "seit": it is used with the present tense when the action continues to the present, e.g. "Ich wohne seit einem Jahr hier".
l:dativ:3:ex0: I have been learning German for a month.
l:dativ:3:ex1: We are talking with the teacher.
l:dativ:3:ex2: The café is located opposite the museum.
l:dativ:3:title: Common Mistakes
l:dativ:intro: Dative prepositions always require the dative case. The dative often marks the recipient, location, or reference of an action.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:body: When describing a fixed position, the noun after a two-way preposition takes the dative. Typical verbs are sein, bleiben, liegen, stehen, sitzen, and hängen (in a state).
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:ex0: The book lies on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:ex1: The cat sleeps under the sofa.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:title: Wo? — Static position
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:body: When describing movement toward a goal, the noun takes the accusative. Typical verbs are gehen, fahren, legen, stellen, setzen, and hängen (as an action).
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:ex0: I put the book on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:ex1: The cat jumps under the sofa.
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:title: Wohin? — Movement to a goal
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:body: Many verb pairs distinguish state and action: liegen/legen, stehen/stellen, sitzen/setzen, hängen/hängen. The case depends not only on the preposition but also on the verb's meaning.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex0: The bottle stands on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex1: I put the bottle on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex2: The picture hangs on the wall.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:title: The verb also decides
l:wechselpraepositionen:3:body: Common contractions include in+dem=im, an+dem=am, in+das=ins, an+das=ans; "nach Hause" and "zu Hause" do not use a two-way preposition. Always ask first: Wo? or Wohin?
l:wechselpraepositionen:3:title: Contractions and typical mistakes
l:wechselpraepositionen:intro: The nine two-way prepositions take the dative when describing a position (Wo?) and the accusative when describing movement toward a destination (Wohin?).
m:akkusativ:summary: These prepositions always require the accusative case. They include durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, and entlang.
m:akkusativ:title: Prepositions with Accusative
m:dativ:summary: The prepositions mit, nach, aus, bei, von, zu, seit, and gegenüber always take the dative case.
m:dativ:title: Prepositions with Dative
m:genitiv:title: Prepositions with Genitive
m:wechselpraepositionen:summary: The nine two-way prepositions (in, an, auf, unter, über, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) take the dative for location (Wo?) and the accusative for direction (Wohin?).
